Hey,
I'm not using the appDir functionality yet so for fixing that issue i had to modify the `next.config.js` by 

* turning off the appDir
 ```json
 experimental: {
    appDir: false
  },
 ```
* forcing ip4 on the server
 ```javascript
 const dns = require('dns');
dns.setDefaultResultOrder("ipv4first");
 ```
I hope it will give you some ideas if it doesn't help you.
I have this issue in next.js version 13.4.13 as well (node 20.4.9). Is there a fix in the pipeline?

I solved this error checkout this code for understanding [ https://github.com/Sumitmaithani/competency-passbook]( https://github.com/Sumitmaithani/competency-passbook) in short you don't need to write full link like http://localhost:3000/ or something in start just start by `/api/whateveryouwant` and use axios for api requests in place of fetch. This solved my problem.

issue.title: 3x more network requests and latency issue on the same project after version upgrade

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

issue.body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
      Platform: linux
      Arch: x64
      Version: #1 SMP Wed May 24 23:46:10 UTC 2023
    Binaries:
      Node: 18.16.0
      npm: 9.5.1
      Yarn: N/A
      pnpm: N/A
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.4.7
      eslint-config-next: 13.4.4
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
      typescript: 5.1.3
```


### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

_No response_

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue or a replay of the bug

-

### To Reproduce

We have a containerised (Docker) Next.js app running on the Kubernetes environment. Hence we need to map the requests from the real world into the container to the app. Monitoring-wise, we use Datadog. 

Till now, we used to use Next.js v12.x, but now we upgraded the project to the latest v13.4.7. After the version upgrade, the network traffic/requests and the latency increased enormously. We have not changed anything in our codebase or infrastructure or anything else; we just upgraded the Next.js version.


### Describe the Bug

With Next.js v12 we got these traces for a request, which is normal:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/df9e00fd-ab24-49ad-9485-5f3d07e9ef35)

But when we upgraded to the latest `v13.4.7`, we got this for the same request:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/336c82cc-4b4a-4d9c-a856-ace7cf43afe4)

The requests were tripled! It isn't visible on the client-side, but only on the APM logging, so on the server-side.

I checked the other Next.js versions between these 2, and it turned out that this issue started happening in `v13.3.5-canary.12`. **The `v13.3.5-canary.11` was still fine.**

Requests before and after the version upgrade:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/a4d2240a-b8e7-4c56-87af-7f7f2f210afb)

Latency before and after the version upgrade:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/e2dfd4c2-b257-4a0c-adb4-6d2186474624)

The new extra GET requests are highlighted with yellow colour as the top resource in terms of requests:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/194c42fb-8535-46d7-a6f8-8a59f100263b)

CPU used by pod
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/7598e118-a731-471f-9703-fbe582f92ab5)

Memory used by pod
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/3d963665-5ec6-4113-a504-25c9db014d9f)

Network stats:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1906302/013574a2-0a24-489a-9d68-4c9cf316e231)


### Expected Behavior

The number of requests should be the same as it was before.

### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

_No response_

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

Azure DevOps
